newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa trims losses, March still 16-mth low.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa trims losses, March still 16-mth low.

text.p: London cocoa futures trimmed some losses but benchmark March still ended at the lowest level in 16 months on origin selling driven by the strength of sterling.
"It is the same story as in the last couple of weeks...the strength of sterling is not helping again," said one trader.
March contract finished the day four stg down at 887 stg a tonne, the lowest level since August 1995, but above a session low of 878.
The contract traded at 880 stg at midday.

Traders said the late recovery was sparked by trade short-covering but a rise from 880 to a high of 888 stg was backed by a light volume. March broke crucial support at 891 on Friday and 883 stg this morning without much hesitation because of the strength of sterling against French franc.
The day's volume was a moderate 4,530 lots.
Chart-wise, the technical picture looked very weak while industry buying interest remained muted. Traders pegged the next major support at 860 area basis March.
Some said the current slump still came as a surprise with cocoa shipments from the origins so far this season continued to trail last season's arrivals.
"This time last year the market was trading at 930-940 stg basis second-month position even though we saw a much larger Ivorian crop," said one.
Analysts and exporters in Abidjan said on Monday Ivorian 1996/97 cocoa crop arrivals stood at around 390,000-400,000 tonnes by mid-December.
This compares with an estimated 540,000 by the same period in 1995.
